subject: Physics 0625 (Demo)
mcq: A car travels 150 m in 6.0 s at a constant speed. What is its speed?
Velocity has both size and direction.
A ball is dropped from rest. Air resistance is negligible. What happens to its acceleration as it falls?
It stays constant at about 9.8 m/s².
In free fall the acceleration is g, which is constant.

What is the weight of a 5.0 kg mass on Earth? (g = 9.8 N/kg)

A force of 20 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.50 m from a pivot. What is the moment of the force?

A motor does 600 J of work in 20 s. What is its power?
A force of 200 N acts on an area of 0.50 m². What is the pressure?
A car of mass 1500 kg travels at 20 m/s. What is its momentum?
Which statement describes the particles in a solid?
close together and vibrating about fixed positions
close together and sliding past each other
By which process can thermal energy travel through a vacuum?
What happens to the temperature of the liquid left behind when some of it evaporates?
The most energetic particles escape, so the average kinetic energy of the rest falls.

A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 4.0 m. What is its speed?
Which electromagnetic wave has the longest wavelength?
Through which of these can sound NOT travel?
A ray of light hits a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle of reflection?
Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
A current of 0.50 A flows through a 12 Ω resistor. What is the potential difference across it?
Two 6.0 Ω resistors are connected in series. What is the combined resistance?
Two 6.0 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the combined resistance?
A current of 2.0 A flows for 30 s. How much charge passes?
A transformer has 200 turns on the primary coil and 50 turns on the secondary coil. The input voltage is 240 V. What is the output voltage?
What is an alpha particle made of?
A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 6 hours. What fraction of the original nuclei remains undecayed after 18 hours?
Approximately how long does the Earth take to orbit the Sun once?
Light from distant galaxies is redshifted. What does this suggest?

cloze.title: Motion and Energy
rows: Speed is the **distance** travelled per unit **time**.
mass
**Velocity** is speed in a given direction, so it is a **vector** quantity.
scalar
The gradient of a distance–time graph gives the **speed** of an object.
force
An object falling freely near the Earth's surface has an **acceleration** of about 9.8 m/s².
momentum
The **weight** of an object is the gravitational force acting on its mass.
density
When a ball falls, gravitational potential energy is converted into **kinetic** energy.
chemical
**Power** is the rate at which work is done.
pressure
The principle of conservation of **energy** states that it cannot be created or destroyed.
charge

cloze.title: Waves and Electricity
rows: The **frequency** of a wave is the number of waves passing a point each second.
amplitude
Light bends towards the normal when it enters glass from air; this is called **refraction**.
diffraction
Sound is a **longitudinal** wave, whereas light is a **transverse** wave.
electromagnetic
Electric **current** is the rate of flow of charge.
voltage
In a **series** circuit, the current is the same at every point.
parallel
A **transformer** only works with an alternating current.
battery
The **resistance** of a wire increases as its length increases.
thickness
